pairs.subject: delivery-guarantees
pairs.evidence: src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/PendingTriggerApprovals.tsx:49 The approval queue this component drives marks a held fire 'approved' with one write and publishes its event with a second, separate write. If the publish fails, the fire reads as approved forever, never ran, and can no longer be retried because it has left 'pending'.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/repos/resources/triggers/fires.rs:134 Resolving a held fire is one conditional compare-and-swap that only one caller can win, and the command publishes only when it wins (won_cas). A double-click cannot fire the event twice.

src-tauri/src/commands/tools/triggers.rs:204 The consume (the status CAS) and its only effect (event_repo::publish into the same SQLite pool, line 210) run as two separate commits. A transaction-taking publish_in exists at events.rs:201, so the two could be one commit.

src-tauri/src/commands/tools/triggers.rs:210 The 'approved' marker is written before this effect and does not depend on it succeeding. A publish error leaves an approved fire with no event, and the status != 'pending' early-out blocks any retry.

src-tauri/db/src/repos/resources/triggers/fires.rs:119 Discarding a held fire leaves the row in place, marked 'rejected' with resolved_at, and that is written at the decision site. Caveat: the UI forgets the row and only shows a toast, so the user never sees the skip again.

src/features/triggers/hooks/useTriggerHistory.ts:130 Replaying a (failed) execution from the history redrives it as a brand-new execution with a random idempotency key. It never sets retry_of_execution_id, although PersonaExecution has that field, so the redrive loses its lineage to the original failure.
